$comment: Implements spec 03 §4 (assessment schemes: slots, learning-area score, component policy, missing-mark policy, rounding, formative observations), §4.1 (period to annual aggregation), §5 (grading scales) and §6 (aggregations, ranking). This file is the schema for assessment.json.
title: Curriculum pack assessment model (assessment.json)
description: Assessment schemes, grading scales, aggregation operators, ranking policy and the period-to-annual rule (spec 03 §4 to §6).

schemes.description: Assessment schemes by level band. Codes are unique within the pack (runtime check).

grading_scales.description: Every scale the pack references from a scheme, aggregation or national assessment (spec 03 §5).

aggregations.description: Overall-result operators such as KCSE best-7, PLE division or the Francophone moyenne (spec 03 §6). Optional for a formative-only pack.

scheme.description: A marks-and-slots scheme or a rubric-observation scheme. The two shapes are mutually exclusive: each branch forbids the other branch's keys (spec 03 §4).

levels.description: Levels the scheme applies to. Codes must resolve to declared levels (runtime check).

slots.description: The assessments that exist in a period and their weight buckets (spec 03 §4: CA1 20, CA2 20, Exam 60). Slot codes are unique within the scheme (runtime check).

grading_scale.description: Scale code applied to the learning-area score, for example waec or kcse_subject (spec 03 §4).

rounding.description: Rounding rules per computation stage. The default is to round only for display and grade lookup (spec 03 §4).

overridable.description: Scheme paths a school may override, for example slots.*.scale_to (spec 03 §4, §2.3).

evidence.description: The only evidence source named in spec 03 §4: teacher rubric observations per outcome, optionally with a photo or note (§9).

observation_scale.description: Scale code used for observation levels, for example cbe_4_level (spec 03 §4, §5).

summative_slots.description: Optional marks-based slots inside a formative scheme, such as an end-of-term test mapped onto the rubric (spec 03 §4). Omit it for a purely observational scheme: with no slots the term result is the teacher's best-fit rubric level over the observed outcomes for each learning area, mapped from observation_scale, and report_shows selects which parts of that judgement are printed. Nothing numeric is computed, so no marks need to be invented.

report_shows.description: What the report card shows for this scheme (spec 03 §4 example; §8.1 rubric_table).

kind.description: Assessment kind from spec 02 §8. The spec 03 §4 examples use cat and end_term.

max.description: Raw maximum for one assessment in this slot, for example CA1 max 20 (spec 03 §4).

scale_to.description: Points this slot contributes after scaling, for example CAT scale_to 30 (spec 03 §4). Scores are stored raw and scaled by the engine.

multi.description: True when the slot collects several assessments, for example all CATs in a term (spec 03 §4).

combine.description: How several assessments in a multi slot are reduced. Spec 03 §4 names mean for multi slots; best_of and sum are the reductions named for components.

max.description: Raw maximum for the assessment (spec 03 §4 example: 100).

maps_to.description: Scale the summative result maps onto, for example cbe_4_level (spec 03 §4).

op.description: How slot results combine into the learning-area score. Spec 03 §4 examples use sum.

of.description: Slot codes that feed the score. Each must be declared in slots (runtime check).

out_of.description: Denominator the learning-area score is expressed out of, for example 100 (spec 03 §4).

missingPolicyMap.description: Missing-mark policy per slot: zero scores it zero; exclude removes it and renormalises the remaining weights; incomplete produces no grade and flags the learner; carry_previous uses the previous period's mark (spec 03 §4). Keys must be slot codes declared in the same scheme (runtime check).

papers.description: How papers are combined: sum raw, scale each to a common maximum then sum, weighted by component weight, or keep the best of several attempts (spec 03 §4).

out_of.description: Denominator the combined paper result is expressed out of, for example 100 (spec 03 §4).

weights.description: Per learning-area component weights, keyed by learning-area code and then component code. Declaring the share here keeps it inside the scheme, where two learning areas that both call a paper P1 cannot collide. Merge rule: a weight declared here wins for that learning area and component; a component's own weight applies when this map does not name it. The resolved weights for one learning area must sum to 1 (runtime check).

best_of.description: How many papers or attempts count when papers is best_of.

stage.description: Computation stage the rule applies to. Spec 03 §4 gives learning_area_score; component_score, period_result and annual are the other stages the engine computes.

mode.description: Rounding mode for this stage. The vocabulary is shared with aggregation.mode; see common.schema.json#/$defs/roundingMode for the canonical meanings and the floor/ceil/truncate mapping.

op.description: A teacher makes the final term judgement from the evidence (spec 03 §4).

suggest.description: Strategy the engine uses to suggest a level. Spec 03 §4 names mode_of_latest_per_outcome; the field stays open because later strategies do not change the shape.

op.description: How period results become an annual result (spec 03 §4.1).

of.description: Period weights as a map of period code to fraction, or a list of period codes. Spec 03 §4.1 example: T1 0.3, T2 0.3, T3 0.4. Weights must sum to 1 (runtime check).

missing.description: What to do when a period has no result. renormalise is the spec 03 §4.1 example and is the annual form of the slot-level exclude policy.

n.description: How many periods count when op is best_of.

schemesSection.description: A standalone schemes fragment, the shape shown in spec 03 §4.

aggregationsSection.description: A standalone aggregations fragment, the shape shown in spec 03 §6.

annualSection.description: A standalone annual fragment, the shape shown in spec 03 §4.1.
